READ-ONLY market research. WebSearch/WebFetch; cite with dates and source grade. Write to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\biz-ideas.md; return a concise summary. No installs, no MCP.

Role: business analyst. Generate ~8 candidate AI/software product ideas that could REALISTICALLY grow into very large (billion-dollar-potential) businesses, built as a product layer on top of frontier AI by a small team with strong agents (NOT training a frontier model). For each candidate: the problem, who pays, current market + named competitors, why-now, the realistic wedge, and the honest risk. Favor areas with real budgets and painful problems (e.g. AI-agent reliability/observability, vertical AI for a regulated industry, dev-tooling, data/retrieval infra, compliance/security automation, workflow automation). Then SCORE and shortlist the best 5 by (market size x pain x feasibility-for-a-small-team x defensibility x time-to-traction). BE HONEST: flag which are crowded, which need capital/regulation, and that "billion-dollar in a short time" is rare — rank by realistic potential, not hype. Note where a claim needs a paid database (Crunchbase/PitchBook/CapIQ) you don't have.

handback.t:
Report written to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\biz-ideas.md (read-only research, WebSearch only, dated 2026-10-05, with sources graded A/B/C).

Candidates (8): (1) agent testing/eval/observability, (2) agent identity and runtime policy, (3) AI back-office for accountants, (4) healthcare RCM denials and prior auth, (5) insurance underwriting/claims niche, (6) compliance evidence automation for a regulated niche, (7) retrieval/context layer, (8) legacy modernization agents. Each entry has problem, payer, competitors, why-now, wedge and honest risk.

Scores (/25): RCM 20; accounting niche 19; regulated-niche compliance 19; agent testing 19; agent identity 19; legacy modernization 18; insurance 17; retrieval 14. These are my judgment, not computed from data.

Shortlist, ranked by realistic potential:
1. Healthcare RCM denials/prior auth, specialty wedge. Biggest measurable budget and outcome pricing. Needs HIPAA, EHR integration and a domain partner.
2. AI back-office for accountants in a niche (local statutory regime or audit-evidence workflow). Fastest path to paying users. Basis, Accrual and Rillet are well funded, so the niche is the only opening.
3. Compliance evidence for mandated frameworks (CMMC/FedRAMP, DORA/NIS2, medical-device QMS). Avoid generic SOC 2, where Vanta and Drata dominate.
4. Domain-specific agent regression testing. Easiest to build with agents but the weakest moat, and generic observability is crowded and open-source-pressured. Likely exit is acquisition.
5. Agent identity/runtime policy. Largest budgets and acquirers (CyberArk to Palo Alto, Astrix to Cisco), but it needs security credibility and likely venture capital.

Runner-up is legacy modernization, services-heavy at first. I excluded customer-support agents (Sierra, Decagon) and horizontal coding assistants as too crowded and capital-heavy.

Honesty flags:
- "Billion-dollar fast" is a rare tail event. A realistic good outcome is $10-100M ARR or an acquisition, and survivorship bias is strong in the named winners.
- Generic infra/observability and retrieval are the most exposed to open source, model vendors and platform bundling.
- The EU AI Act high-risk deadline slipped from Aug 2026 to Dec 2027 (Annex III) and Aug 2028 (Annex I), per Regulation 2026/1744 (A-grade law-firm sources). That weakens "AI Act panic" as a near-term driver.
- All valuations, ARR and round figures are from news/aggregator pages and need Crunchbase, PitchBook or CapIQ to confirm. Treat the Cursor "$60B SpaceX acquisition" and the Ensemble "~$12B" deal as unverified. Market-size numbers ($4.35B AI observability, $1.3B compliance automation) come from low-grade sources.
- Pairing and extra advice in the file: validate with 15-20 buyer interviews, pre-sell outcome-priced pilots, and start as an agent-assisted service before productizing.
